title: Obex calculates its own rebate but Operational GovOps holds a hard block on distributing the resulting surplus
content:
The Upkeep Rebate routine protocol runs in three steps. Obex "keeps all tokens of other Agents it holds in its SubProxy account" (A.6.1.1.5.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.1); "When paying Ecosystem Upkeep fees, Obex deducts the rebate from the fees it pays" (A.6.1.1.5.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.2); and then A.6.1.1.5.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.3: "Operational GovOps reviews Obex's calculation of the rebate before executing a return of surplus to token holders. In the event of any issues, Operational GovOps **cannot** execute the distribution."

The separation of duties is exact. The party with the incentive to overstate the rebate computes it; a different party verifies it; and the verifier's power is a hard block, phrased as an incapacity rather than a discretion. "Cannot execute" leaves no room for GovOps to proceed under protest.

The holding requirement in step one is what makes verification tractable. Concentrating all other-Agent tokens in the SubProxy account gives the reviewer a single, publicly observable address to check the claimed holdings against, turning an audit into an on-chain lookup.

The deadlock rule completes the mechanism: GovOps "must post an explanation on the Sky Forum … and work with Obex to resolve the disagreement," and unresolved disputes "must be escalated to Core GovOps." A block therefore cannot become a silent, permanent freeze — it must be explained publicly and has a defined route out at the ecosystem level. This is the only dispute-escalation path spelled out anywhere in Obex's Primitives, and it is notably more complete than the Root Edit veto, which has none.
description: GovOps reviews the calculation and cannot execute distribution if it finds issues; it must then post a public explanation and, if disagreement persists, escalate to Core GovOps.
